licenses.issuingAuthority: Department of Labour, Employment, Training & Skill Development (Inspector of Factories / Deputy Chief Inspector of Factories / Chief Inspector of Factories), Government of Jharkhand

portal.name: Jharkhand Single Window System / Shramadhan portal

timeline.basis: Official procedure: 12-day sub-deadline for the Inspector to forward recommendation, within an overall 30-day processing window for complete applications
timeline.text: The current online procedure stipulates a 30-day processing timeline for a complete factory license application, with the Inspector of Factories required to forward their recommendation within 12 days of submission.

documents: Completed Form No. 2 (submitted via the online portal)
Proof of prescribed license fee payment (challan)
Registered sale deed, registered lease deed, or registered rent agreement (proof of possession)
Owner consent and address proof (for leased or rented premises)
Approved building or site plan documents (where applicable)
Consent to Establish or Consent to Operate from the Jharkhand State Pollution Control Board
Identity and address proof of the occupier
Identity and address proof of the factory manager
Name and address of the designated person managing affairs (government/local authority units)
Factory/project report
Detailed description of the manufacturing process
Details of machinery and total installed power capacity
Board list, MOA, AOA, and Board resolution appointing the occupier under Section 2(n) (public limited companies)
Partnership deed and list of partners (partnership firms)
Any other specific documents requested by the Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspector, or Inspector

deemedApproval.text: No automatic deemed approval currently exists after the 30-day processing period elapses; the ED recommends introducing statutory deemed approval for complete, low-risk applications with safety exclusions and post-approval inspection/cancellation powers.

validity.text: The Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025 establish a minimum license validity of one year, with longer-term options also offered; the issued license specifies its own validity period, and one-year licenses require annual renewal via the Shramadhan portal.

fees.text: Calculated under Schedule-A based on total rated machinery/plant capacity (HP) and maximum workers on any single day; examples: Nil HP = ₹530 (up to 20 workers)/₹2,060 (up to 50)/₹2,380 (up to 100); Up to 10 HP = ₹1,190/₹2,110/₹2,900 for the same worker slabs. Electricity generating/transforming/transmitting stations use a separate KW-based schedule (Schedule-B/C). The 2025 amendment set a standardized license amendment fee of ₹1,000. The Shramadhan portal's automated calculator determines the exact fee.

steps.title: Login & Selection
steps.note: Applicant logs into the Jharkhand Single Window/Shramadhan portal and selects Factory Act registration and grant of license.

steps.title: Application Submission
steps.note: Applicant completes Form No. 2, uploads documents, and pays the license fee online.

steps.title: Scrutiny & Deficiency
steps.note: Receiving office scrutinizes the application; deficiencies communicated electronically for resubmission.

steps.title: Forwarding
steps.note: Complete application forwarded electronically to the Inspector of Factories.

steps.title: Review & Inspection
steps.note: Inspector reviews the application and conducts a site inspection; allocation is managed automatically by the departmental system.

steps.title: Recommendation
steps.note: Inspector records findings/recommendations and forwards the case to the Deputy Chief Inspector.

steps.title: Approval & Issuance
steps.note: Competent authority approves; license issued electronically with SMS/status notification.

ed.location: Department of Industry, Nepal House, Single Window Office, Ranchi

remarks: The Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025 govern the current validity and fee structures.
Discretionary documents may be requested by the Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspector, or Inspector for a particular factory, beyond the standard document list.

findings.text: The factory license service is fully digitized through the Shramadhan/Jharkhand Single Window portal, covering application, document upload, fee payment, status tracking, deficiency handling, and license issuance; the only physical component is the site inspection.
The official procedure stipulates 12 days for the Inspector to forward their recommendation, within an overall 30-day timeline for processing complete applications.
There is no statutory deemed-approval mechanism; the license is not issued automatically even if the 30-day SLA lapses.

Recommended introducing statutory deemed approval for complete, low-risk applications after the SLA lapses, with safety exclusions, post-approval inspection protocols, and authority to cancel for non-compliance.

A significant compliance burden persists from repeated submission and manual verification of information already held by other departments, such as land ownership records, project details, and environmental clearances.
Recommended shifting from manual, redundant document uploads to system-to-system verification with authoritative government databases for land, pollution, and building approval statuses.
Proposed a 'Master Factory Profile' to enable reuse of verified data, streamlining document compilation for future applications and amendments.
Proposed replacing repeated deficiency cycles with a single, consolidated deficiency memo to give clearer, actionable feedback.
Proposed deploying an automated Schedule-A/B/C fee calculator to ensure transparency and accuracy in variable fee assessments.

Jharkhand uses a risk-based inspection framework: low-risk establishments get inspection exemptions, medium-risk face third-party certification and joint verification, and high-risk face mandatory departmental technical/site inspections.
Recommended an expedited, simplified renewal process for established factories with clean compliance records.
The 2025 amendment standardized the license amendment fee at ₹1,000 and set Schedule-A fee slabs based on HP and worker count.
SMS-based proactive status notifications are used throughout the process for transparency.

Post-approval compliance requires maintaining statutory registers/returns, safety/health standards, and securing license amendments for any changes to address, occupier/manager, workforce size, or machinery/power capacity.

gaps.text: Full fee schedule is not disclosed beyond the Nil HP and Up to 10 HP example rows; amounts for higher HP/worker slabs are only described as 'subject to higher notified fees' without figures.
The document does not specify what happens to the 30-day overall timeline if scrutiny/deficiency resubmission cycles extend processing beyond that window.

The Shramadhan Comprehensive Labour Management System provides a unified digital platform covering the entire factory regulation lifecycle (registration, licensing, renewal, amendment, inspection, fee, communication).
ED recommends a legally notified 'deemed approval' mechanism for complete, low-risk applications, including safety exclusions and post-approval inspection/cancellation authority.

Exact criteria or thresholds distinguishing low/medium/high-risk factory classification are described only qualitatively (manufacturing process, hazardous substances, explosion potential, population density), without quantified thresholds.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Department of Labour, Employment, Training & Skill Development (Inspector of Factories / Deputy Chief Inspector of Factories / Chief Inspector of Factories), Government of Jharkhand

timeline.basis: 30-day statutory disposal period for factory/shed and building plan applications, consistent with the national ServicePlus listing for permission to construct/extend/utilize a building as a factory
timeline.text: The prescribed processing timeline for Factory Plan Approval in Jharkhand is 30 days; where clarification is required, the applicant is notified and the processing cycle resumes once requested information is submitted.

documents: PAN Card and address proof
Comprehensive Project Report
Land ownership/tenancy proof: registered sale deed, registered lease deed, or registered rent agreement (owner consent and address proof where applicable)
Flowchart of the manufacturing process with a brief written description
Complete list of plant and machinery to be installed
Factory Plan drawn to scale, in CAD format
Site Plan showing surroundings, existing buildings, structures, roads, and drainage
Building Design: plans, elevations, and cross-sections showing lighting/ventilation, fire-escape layouts, plant/machinery placement, and aisles/passageways

deemedApproval.text: No automatic deemed approval currently exists upon expiry of the 30-day period; any deemed-approval model would require express statutory notification or rule amendment, with safeguards such as completeness validation, SLA monitoring, post-approval audit, and risk-based exclusions.

validity.text: A one-time approval rather than a renewable license, with no annual validity period; the approved plan governs construction, reconstruction, extension, or commissioning until compliance conditions change, at which point a revised or amended approval is required.

fees.text: Calculated as a share of the applicable Factory License fee slab: 25% of the Factory License fee for new factories, or 10% of the applicable fee for extension/reconstruction; the final payable amount depends on the relevant license fee slab and application type.

steps.title: Secondary Inspection (as applicable)
steps.note: Deputy Chief Inspector reviews and may conduct a supplementary site visit if necessary.

steps.title: Approval/Recommendation Path

steps.title: Final Issuance
steps.note: For applications with 50+ employees, the Chief Inspector issues the approval electronically with conditions.

steps.title: Compliance
steps.note: Applicant must construct and operate strictly per the approved plans and stipulated conditions.

ed.location: Department of Industry, Nepal House, Single Window Office, Ranchi

remarks: Technical drawings (factory plan, site plan, building design) must be submitted in the prescribed digital format, with the factory plan in CAD format.
Any modification to the approved site, building layout, machinery placement, or other regulated parameters requires a revised or amended approval.

findings.text: Factory Plan Approval is entirely digital via the Jharkhand Single Window System; the only physical components are the prescribed site visits/inspections by the Inspector of Factories and, where applicable, the Deputy Chief Inspector.
The official 30-day disposal timeline applies, consistent with the national ServicePlus listing for permission to construct/extend/utilize a building as a factory.
No deemed approval currently exists after the 30-day period; introducing one would require statutory notification and robust safeguards.
ED recommends statutory deemed approval for eligible low-risk, complete applications via legal notification, with safety exclusions and post-approval audits.
The primary redundancy is repetitive submission of applicant identity, land/ownership status, and standard factory particulars already held in state government databases.
Recommended integrating with existing land, pollution, and identity databases to eliminate redundant document uploads for non-technical data.
Proposed a reusable 'factory/project profile' that retains core data to prevent applicants re-entering information for future requests.
Recommended linking approved plans electronically to subsequent Factory License applications for a seamless 'apply once' experience.
Recommended replacing iterative, fragmented clarification cycles with a single, consolidated deficiency memo.

Risk-based scrutiny model: low-risk projects receive streamlined scrutiny with targeted inspections, medium-risk use a hybrid of third-party certification plus departmental verification, and high-risk projects undergo mandatory rigorous technical/site review.
Recommended clearly displaying the full fee calculation prior to the payment gateway to improve transparency.
Automated SMS notifications are issued to applicants at every key stage of the processing cycle.
Recommended standardized digital templates and automated validation checklists for technical drawing submissions to reduce manual scrutiny errors.
Approved plans require strict adherence during construction; any changes to site, building layout, or machinery placement require a revised or amended approval.

gaps.text: Exact rupee fee amounts are not given — the fee is only expressed as 25%/10% of the Factory License fee slab, with no worked examples provided.
The document does not specify how many of the 30 days are consumed if the Deputy Chief Inspector conducts a secondary site visit.
Risk-based inspection framework tailoring scrutiny depth (low/medium/high-risk) to project risk, administered via the Shramadhan portal.
ED proposes linking Factory Plan Approval records directly to subsequent Factory License applications for an 'apply once' experience.
The document gives the '50 employees' threshold for routing approval authority but does not elaborate on how proposed employment is verified or defined at this stage.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Authority administering the Jharkhand Building Plan Approval and Management System (BPAMS), as discussed by the Department of Labour's Assistant Town Planner; for industrial areas, the Jharkhand Industrial Area Development Authority (JIADA) follows its own SOP

portal.name: Jharkhand Building Plan Approval and Management System (BPAMS)

timeline.basis: Standard: authority must conduct a site inspection within 15 days of a properly completed application; JIADA SOP: accelerated 8-day sequence (7 days inspection + 1 day certificate issuance); anecdotal practitioner feedback cited an unofficial 2-3 week turnaround
timeline.text: The authority is mandated to inspect the site within 15 days of a properly completed application; under JIADA's SOP a faster 8-day process applies; some interview feedback suggested 2-3 weeks informally, but this is explicitly flagged as not an official figure.

documents: Notice of completion
Three copies of as-built building plans
Prescribed fee of ₹1,000
Approved building plan and building permit approval letter
Structural engineer's safety and stability certificate
Fire-safety installation certificate (where applicable)
Evidence of utility connections (drainage, water supply, electricity linked to public systems)
Completion certificate from the concerned architect
Ownership and property documents
licenses.documentsNote: Application requires active involvement of Licensed Technical Professionals (LTPs) such as architects and engineers, who prepare and certify the as-built plans and safety documentation.

deemedApproval.text: The Jharkhand Building Bye-laws 2016 establish a deemed-approval mechanism: if the authority does not dispose of the (resubmitted, affidavit-backed) application within 15 days, occupancy is deemed granted.

validity.text: The Occupancy Certificate acts as a permanent authorization for building usage rather than an annually renewable license, so no periodic renewal is required; a fresh approval may be needed if the structure undergoes significant material alteration or a change of purpose.

fees.text: A base processing fee of ₹1,000 accompanies the notice of completion; additional charges related to project-specific building plans, site inspections, or NOCs may apply depending on the development.

steps.title: Application Submission
steps.note: Applicant or LTP submits the completion/occupancy application via BPAMS once construction is complete.

steps.title: Document Upload
steps.note: Notice of completion, as-built plans, fee, stability/fire-safety certificates, and utility-connection evidence are uploaded.

steps.title: Scrutiny
steps.note: The submitted application and associated NOCs/approvals are formally scrutinized.

steps.title: Site Inspection Scheduling
steps.note: Authority team is required to visit the site within 15 days of receiving a properly completed application.

steps.title: Site Inspection
steps.note: Officials inspect compliance with the approved building plan and structural, fire, life-safety, and utility requirements.

steps.title: Issuance / Deemed Grant
steps.note: OC issued if compliant; if not disposed within 15 days, occupancy is deemed granted provided required affidavits were submitted.

remarks: JIADA (Jharkhand Industrial Area Development Authority) areas follow a distinct, faster SOP for OC processing (8 days) compared to the general 15-day standard.

Invoking deemed approval requires the applicant to submit necessary affidavits confirming compliance with safety and building standards; this mechanism is distinct from third-party architect/engineer certification.

findings.text: The Occupancy Certificate process follows a hybrid model: the entire administrative lifecycle is digitized via BPAMS, but a physical site inspection remains mandatory for all building categories.
The standard official procedure requires a site inspection within 15 days of a properly completed application.
A JIADA-specific SOP cites an accelerated 8-day process (7 days inspection + 1 day issuance), which differs from the general 15-day standard timeline described elsewhere in the same ED.
Some interview feedback suggested an unofficial 2-3 week turnaround, which the ED explicitly flags as anecdotal and not a confirmed statutory figure.
The Jharkhand Building Bye-laws 2016 provide a deemed-approval safeguard: occupancy is deemed granted if the authority fails to act within 15 days of a compliant, affidavit-backed resubmission.
Risk-based inspection model: site inspection is compulsory for all categories, but medium- and high-risk categories additionally require mandatory third-party and joint inspections.
Process fragmentation causes high friction due to the need for manual coordination across multiple agencies and technical professionals (LTPs).
Potential duplication occurs when the same completion and safety data are certified or scrutinized multiple times across different stages or departments.
Applicants face operational hurdles in inspection scheduling, assembling technical reports/NOCs, and the iterative nature of document submission.
Recommended transitioning to a single, unified online 'completion-cum-occupancy' application to replace fragmented submissions.
Recommended auto-populating application data from previously approved building plans to reduce manual input and errors.
Recommended joint, coordinated site inspections involving all relevant agencies simultaneously, rather than separate individual agency visits.
Recommended consolidating verification of all required NOCs within the central BPAMS system.
Recommended standardized digital inspection checklists requiring upload of digital evidence (e.g., photos/videos) for transparency and consistency.
Recommended expanding third-party architect/engineer certification for eligible low-risk buildings to accelerate the approval process.

gaps.text: Timeline figures differ within the same ED: a standard 15-day site-inspection mandate, a JIADA accelerated 8-day SOP, and an anecdotal, explicitly unofficial 2-3 week turnaround mentioned by interviewees.

The issuing authority/department is not clearly stated: the header lists 'Department of Labour' while the content describes a town-planning/building-plan process (BPAMS) and separately references JIADA for industrial areas.
Whether the applicant themselves must visit any physical office (as opposed to only LTPs/officials visiting the site) is not explicitly addressed.

BPAMS provides a centralized digital workflow and repository for occupancy inspection checklists/resources, with risk-based recognition of accredited third-party architects/engineers for eligible cases.
ED recommends a single, unified 'completion-cum-occupancy' online application to replace the current fragmented submissions across multiple agencies.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Department of Labour, Employment, Training & Skill Development (Inspector of Factories, with Deputy Chief Inspector/Chief Inspector notified), Government of Jharkhand

portal.name: Jharkhand Single Window System / Shramadhan portal

timeline.basis: Official 30-day processing window commencing upon submission of a complete renewal application and fee payment
timeline.text: The official Jharkhand renewal procedure stipulates a 30-day processing window from submission of a complete application and fee payment; the processing cycle resumes immediately once any requested clarification is received.

documents: Form No. 2 (online renewal application)
Prescribed annual renewal fee (payment proof)

Updated supporting documents for any changed particulars (e.g., occupier/manager, factory address, or production capacity) — only if changes occurred, or if the department requests specific clarification

deemedApproval.text: There is no provision for automatic deemed renewal upon expiry of the 30-day service period; the 30-day timeline governs Inspector review and issuance, but renewal is not granted automatically solely because the period has elapsed.

validity.text: The Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025 establish a minimum license validity of one year, with options for longer durations; the license remains valid for the term on the issued document, and one-year license holders must renew for the subsequent licensing year.

fees.text: Calculated under the 2025 annual fee structure based on rated machinery/plant capacity (HP) and maximum workers employed; examples up to 500 HP: up to 20 workers ₹28,510; up to 50 workers ₹35,640; up to 100 workers ₹37,620; up to 250 workers ₹39,600; up to 500 workers ₹43,560. remarks: The 2025 amendment to the Jharkhand Factories Rules governs the current renewal fee schedule and minimum one-year validity.
The Deputy Chief Inspector and Chief Inspector are automatically notified upon license renewal issuance.

findings.text: Factory license renewal is designed as a fully electronic end-to-end process via the Shramadhan/Single Window portal, intended to require no physical touch points.
Site inspections for renewal are optional and risk-based rather than mandatory for every applicant, consistent with the state's risk-based inspection framework.
Applicants are not required to repeatedly upload documents already on file and unchanged — only updated or newly relevant information must be resubmitted.
The official procedure stipulates a 30-day processing window from submission of a complete application and fee payment.
There is no provision for automatic deemed renewal upon expiry of the 30-day period.
Recommended a statutory framework for deemed renewal, legally notified for eligible low-risk factories with clean compliance histories and unchanged operational particulars.
The primary administrative burden is redundant submission/verification of information already held in the existing factory license record (land, project, incorporation, technical records).
Recommended linking the existing license database directly to the renewal portal to auto-populate details, requiring manual entry only for changed fields.
Recommended a document repository retaining previously verified documents, limiting new uploads to expired or changed items only.
Recommended a dynamic fee calculator that automatically computes the annual renewal fee from current worker counts and machinery capacity.
Recommended issuing a single, comprehensive deficiency notice rather than fragmented clarification requests.
Recommended proactive automated reminders before license expiry, plus application-aging alerts for both applicant and department.
Recommended embedding an 'amendment link' within the renewal portal so occupier/manager or other detail changes can be made without a separate parallel application.
SMS notifications keep applicants informed at every stage of the renewal process.

gaps.text: The full renewal fee table is only given for 'up to 500 HP' examples; amounts for higher HP slabs are not specified in the document.
Criteria determining when a renewal site inspection is 'required' under the risk-based framework are not detailed beyond general risk categorization.
End-to-end online renewal workflow that reuses existing license data to avoid redundant document re-upload for unchanged particulars.
ED proposes a conditional/statutory deemed-renewal mechanism for low-risk factories with clean compliance records and unchanged operational particulars.
No figure is given for how long deficiency/clarification resubmission cycles typically add to the 30-day renewal timeline.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Urban Local Body approval authority (Nagar Nigam/Nagar Parishad/Nagar Panchayat/NAC), under the Urban Development & Housing Department, Government of Jharkhand

portal.name: Municipal (Trade) License Management System / Single Window portal

timeline.basis: 2017 regulation: provisional license within 1 day under trust-and-verify; final license without inspection within 9 days; final license with inspection within 22 working days (inspection report due in 10 working days, decision within a further 3 working days)
timeline.text: A provisional license is issued within 1 day under the trust-and-verify approach; a final license without inspection is issued within 9 days; where a site inspection is required, the final license is issued within 22 working days.

documents: Valid identity proof of the trade applicant
Premises proof if owned: land possession certificate, allotment order, revenue rent, sale deed, correction slip, or updated holding-tax receipt
Premises proof if rented/leased: valid lease/rent agreement, or an electricity bill registered in the applicant's name
Partnership deed or agreement (for partnership firms)
Certificate of incorporation or registration (for companies)
Applicable licenses, NOCs, or clearances required by the nature of the business, with the prescribed declaration or affidavit
licenses.documentsNote: The ED also describes renewal-specific documentation (current-year holding/property tax receipt plus the previous municipal trade license, and conditional NOCs) under the same 'Documentation Required' theme — this is covered in the TLR entry.

deemedApproval.text: The Jharkhand Municipal Trade License Regulation, 2017 provides deemed approval: if an application is not processed within 9 days (no inspection) or 22 working days (with inspection), it is treated as deemed approved.

validity.text: Valid for 12 months from issuance; renewal applications must be submitted at least one month before expiry; renewals generally do not require inspection, though the municipal authority may conduct random post-renewal inspections.

fees.text: Annual fee based on built-up area of commercial premises: up to 100 sq. ft. ₹300; 101-500 sq. ft. ₹500; 501-1,000 sq. ft. ₹1,500; above 1,000 sq. ft. ₹2,500. Fee schedules are subject to revision by individual ULBs; no verified official figure exists for any additional consultant charges discussed informally.

steps.note: Applicant submits application via the Municipal License Management System or Single Window portal, uploads documents, and pays the fee online.

steps.title: License Issuance
steps.note: A provisional license may be issued under the 2017 trust-and-verify approach, with final approval following successful verification.

ed.location: Department of Industry, Nepal House, Single window office, Ranchi

remarks: The Jharkhand Municipal Act, 2011 is the primary legislation empowering municipalities to levy trade license fees; the Jharkhand Municipal Trade License Regulation, 2017 is the governing procedural framework for all notified ULBs (Nagar Nigams, Nagar Parishads, Nagar Panchayats/NACs).
Any proposed removal of duplicative requirements must be explicitly mapped against the Jharkhand Municipal Act, 2011 and the Municipal Trade License Regulation, 2017, to ensure legal validity.

findings.text: The application process is fully digital via the Municipal/Trade License Management System or Single Window portal, with mandatory document uploads, online fee payment, and real-time status tracking.

The 2017 regulation establishes a four-tier internal approval workflow: primary verification (dealing assistant), technical verification (section head), site inspection if required (Tax Daroga/inspector), and final review (approval authority).
While initial application and fee payment are online, manual intervention is still required for internal reporting and physical site inspections.
Under the 2017 regulation's 'trust-and-verify' approach, a provisional license can be issued within 1 day, with final approval following successful verification.
Final license is issued within 9 days without inspection, or within 22 working days when inspection is required (inspection report due in 10 working days, decision within a further 3 working days).
Deemed-approval provision under the 2017 regulation grants automatic approval if the ULB fails to dispose of the application within the mandated 9- or 22-day timeframe.
Applicants are often required to repeatedly submit documentation already available in ULB records or accessible via integrated government portals.
Applications are frequently marked 'pending' due to document upload quality issues or delays in obtaining inter-departmental clearances and technical reports.
The requirement for multiple licenses/NOCs for a single establishment leads to redundant collection of the same establishment details across different applications.
Manual file movement to central offices and repetitive verification steps significantly extend overall processing times.
Although the 2017 regulation does not mandate routine inspections for renewals, the continued practice of physical inspection for every renewal cycle is flagged as redundant.

Risk-based classification ('hazardous'/'non-hazardous') is referenced in documentation, but there is insufficient evidence of a comprehensive formal risk matrix currently integrated into the trade license approval process.
Recommended a formal low/medium/high risk-based matrix using criteria such as environmental impact, fire/food-safety risk, hazardous materials use, and premises scale, to target inspections.
Recommended unifying the portal with departmental databases (Fire, Health, Environment) for automatic validation and auto-population, eliminating redundant submissions.
Recommended an 'automated statutory clock' that auto-generates the deemed-approval notification once the 9-day/22-working-day deadline is crossed.
Recommended a single, comprehensive 'deficiency memo'/checklist for rejected or returned applications, instead of piecemeal communication.

gaps.text: No verified or official consultant-fee figure exists despite 'discussions regarding potential consultant charges' being mentioned; the ED explicitly flags this as unconfirmed.
A formal risk-based classification matrix for TLA is referenced only as a documentation category ('hazardous'/'non-hazardous'); actual criteria/thresholds are not established in current practice.
Fee schedules are described as 'subject to revision by individual ULBs' without specifying how applicants learn the current ULB-specific fee short of checking the portal at application time.
The 'trust-and-verify' approach allows a 1-day provisional license with later verification, reducing time-to-start for businesses.
ED recommends expanding the trust-and-verify model so provisional licenses are issued within one day for low-risk businesses generally, deferring detailed verification.
